title: Exclude illiquid prices
instructions: Return ticker prices where volume is at least {minvol} and price is strictly greater than {minprice}, sorted by price descending.
hint: Work inside out. Each comparison builds one Boolean per ticker, inclusive for ge and exclusive for gt.

explanation.meaning: Each comparison builds one Boolean per ticker, inclusive for ge and exclusive for gt.
Keep rows satisfying BOTH checks.
Extract the two columns and then rank surviving names by price.

title: Ticker lookup table
instructions: Create one row per symbol with its total quantity, indexed by ticker and ordered alphabetically.
hint: Work inside out. Collapse all trade records for each ticker into one quantity total.

explanation.meaning: Collapse all trade records for each ticker into one quantity total.
Convert the ticker column into the semantic row index.
Sort by ticker label, not by the total quantity.

title: Repair a price feed
instructions: Forward-fill missing prices, then return the most recent 6 observation rows.
hint: Work inside out. Fill each missing entry using the most recent earlier price in that asset. This is causal; bfill would import future data.

explanation.meaning: Fill each missing entry using the most recent earlier price in that asset. This is causal; bfill would import future data.
Keep the final six dates after filling the gaps.

title: Price returns without hidden fills
instructions: Calculate simple asset returns from prices without implicitly filling missing observations. Drop dates containing any missing return.
hint: Work inside out. For each asset compute P_t/P_(t-1)-1; leaving missing prices missing avoids artificial zero-return observations.

explanation.meaning: For each asset compute P_t/P_(t-1)-1; leaving missing prices missing avoids artificial zero-return observations.
Delete dates without a complete cross-sectional return vector.

title: Data completeness report
instructions: Return a descending Series of non-missing price observations for each asset.
hint: Work inside out. Count valid time points independently in each column, ignoring NaNs.

explanation.meaning: Count valid time points independently in each column, ignoring NaNs.
Place assets with the strongest history first.

title: Find incomplete histories
instructions: Return a Boolean DataFrame identifying missing-price cells, but only for dates on which at least one price is missing.
hint: Work inside out. Build one Boolean per date and asset, true exactly when an observation is missing.

explanation.meaning: Build one Boolean per date and asset, true exactly when an observation is missing.
For each date, test whether at least one of its assets is missing.
Use that date-level mask to keep only rows with incomplete cross-sectional data.

title: MultiIndex research panel
instructions: Index the panel by date then ticker, sort both levels, and return only ret and volume columns.
hint: Work inside out. Convert two columns into a hierarchical index so every (date,ticker) pair is an address.

explanation.meaning: Convert two columns into a hierarchical index so every (date,ticker) pair is an address.
Sort both index levels, enabling predictable date/ticker slicing.
Keep only measured return and volume, without losing the MultiIndex.

title: Instrument history from a panel
instructions: Return AAPL date-by-date close and return as a two-column DataFrame, indexed by date.
hint: Work inside out. Give date and ticker index levels distinct meanings.

explanation.meaning: Give date and ticker index levels distinct meanings.
Cross-section the ticker dimension, leaving only the date index.
Retain both requested series in a DataFrame.

title: Restore canonical ticker order
instructions: Create a date-by-ticker close-price matrix whose columns appear in the order JPM, NVDA, MSFT, AAPL.
hint: Work inside out. Turn long (date,ticker) rows into a two-axis price matrix.

explanation.meaning: Turn long (date,ticker) rows into a two-axis price matrix.
Rearrange columns by the desired economic order, not alphabetically; absent labels would introduce NaNs.

title: Outlier clipping
instructions: Cap each signal at -{cap} and +{cap}, then return only days whose capped signal is strictly positive.
hint: Work inside out. Apply symmetric limits to each signal without changing its index.

explanation.meaning: Apply symmetric limits to each signal without changing its index.
Build the Boolean mask on the clipped Series itself; lambda passes the current object into the selection.

title: Screen a long panel
instructions: From Tech names with volume >= {minimum}, keep date, ticker, volume and sort within date by ticker.
hint: Work inside out. Evaluate a row filter using column names directly, producing an index-aligned subset.

explanation.meaning: Evaluate a row filter using column names directly, producing an index-aligned subset.
Project only the requested columns.
Sort first by date and then by ticker inside each date.

title: Keep only valid returns
instructions: Return the daily return Series, setting returns of stocks with volume below {minimum} to NaN instead of dropping tickers.
hint: Work inside out. Retain each return where its ticker passes the volume test. Rows that fail become NaN; the index stays unchanged.

explanation.meaning: Retain each return where its ticker passes the volume test. Rows that fail become NaN; the index stays unchanged.
Inclusive comparison constructs the condition using a different column.

title: Join asset volume to ticker metadata
instructions: Build one row per ticker with its sector and total traded volume, indexed and sorted by ticker.
hint: Work inside out. Build a unique ticker-to-sector metadata table.

explanation.meaning: Build a unique ticker-to-sector metadata table.
Build a second table of total asset volumes.
Join two unique key tables; validate prevents accidental row multiplication.
Use ticker labels as the final semantic index.

title: Fallback quote source
instructions: For each date, return MSFT price if present, otherwise AAPL price, as a date-indexed Series.
hint: Work inside out. Keep primary MSFT quotes unless missing, then take the aligned AAPL value as fallback.

explanation.meaning: Keep primary MSFT quotes unless missing, then take the aligned AAPL value as fallback.
Series are matched by date index, NOT by bare array position.

title: Convert returns matrix to long panel
instructions: Transform date-indexed asset return matrix into a long DataFrame with date, ticker and ret columns.
hint: Work inside out. Restore date as a normal column rather than an index label.

explanation.meaning: Restore date as a normal column rather than an index label.
Unpivot four asset columns into ticker labels and ret values, yielding one row per date/asset pair.

title: Stack/unstack round trip
instructions: Stack the return matrix into a date-and-ticker MultiIndex Series and unstack it back into a DataFrame with original column order.
hint: Work inside out. Move the asset column axis into a second level of the row index.

explanation.meaning: Move the asset column axis into a second level of the row index.
Move that ticker index level back into columns; the result is again a date-by-asset DataFrame.
